param_input_item.param_description: Field size: a scalar for a square field, or a [rows cols] vector.
Number of noise cells across the field (default 8). Higher values give finer features.
Seed of the pseudo-random generator (default 0). The same seed reproduces the same field.
If true, sample a periodic lattice so opposite edges match without post-processing (default false).

param_output_item.param_description: The generated field, a rows-by-cols double matrix normalized to [0, 1].

description.p: Generate a field of Perlin gradient noise, the classic smoothly varying coherent noise. Random gradient vectors are placed on an integer lattice and their contributions blended with a quintic fade curve, giving a natural cloud-like field normalized to [0, 1]. With 'seamless' true, the lattice is periodic and suitable for tileable textures. Use it directly or as the basis of fractal composition (see tessera.fbm).

xmldoc.bibliography: M. Hendrikx, S. Meijer, J. van der Velden, A. Iosup, Procedural Content Generation for Games: A Survey, ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications and Applications 9(1), 2013. DOI 10.1145/2422956.2422957.

example_item.example_item_data: R = tessera.perlin(256, 'frequency', 8, 'seed', 1, 'seamless', true); imagesc(R); axis image off; colormap gray
